title: Мужской разговор у бара  (Guy Talk at the Bar)

segments.t: Plagued by guilt over his recurring dreams about Vika, Denis approaches his friend Kostya at the bar for advice. Kostya laughs and tells Denis to enjoy his harmless dreams—right as Nastya walks up behind him and hears Kostya bragging about dreaming of a movie star. Let's listen to their conversation in Russian.
Слушай, Костя, у тебя такое бывало?
Я очень сильно люблю нашу Катю.
А во сне вижу совсем другую женщину.
Скажи, это вообще нормально или нет?
Брат, у меня Настя хочет второго ребёнка.
А у тебя просто обычный сон.
Мне кажется, что я её обманываю.
Может, лучше рассказать ей всю правду?
Ты что, дурак? Это же просто сон!
Мне однажды снилась красивая известная актриса.
Вообще-то у этой актрисы шестеро детей.
Настя, мне этот сон совсем не понравился!
Now let's break down Denis and Kostya's conversation at the bar line by line.
Слушай, Костя, у тебя такое бывало?
'Listen, Kostya, has this ever happened to you?' An frequentative neuter past verb with a possessive phrase asks about past experience.
Я очень сильно люблю нашу Катю.
'I love our Katya very much.' Denis affirms his feelings using a first-person singular present verb and animate accusative name.
А во сне вижу совсем другую женщину.
'But in my dreams I see a completely different woman.' An adversative conjunction contrasts his waking love with the woman appearing in his sleep.
Скажи, это вообще нормально или нет?
'Tell me, is that normal at all or not?' He asks anxiously using a neuter short predicate adjective meaning normal.
Брат, у меня Настя хочет второго ребёнка.
'Bro, my Nastya wants a second child.' Kostya compares Denis's minor worry to his own domestic standoff at home.
А у тебя просто обычный сон.
'And what you have is just an ordinary dream.' He dismisses the dream as harmless using a masculine nominative singular noun phrase.
Мне кажется, что я её обманываю.
'It feels to me like I am deceiving her.' Sensitive Denis still feels guilty, using an imperfective present verb meaning deceiving.
Может, лучше рассказать ей всю правду?
'Maybe it is better to tell her the whole truth?' A comparative predicate adverb introduces a perfective infinitive and dative pronoun.
Ты что, дурак? Это же просто сон!
'What, are you crazy? It is just a dream!' Kostya warns him never to confess a dream about another woman to his girlfriend.
Мне однажды снилась красивая известная актриса.
'I once dreamed about a beautiful famous actress.' To prove his point, Kostya boasts about dreaming of a famous Hollywood star.
Вообще-то у этой актрисы шестеро детей.
'Actually, that actress has six children.' Walking up behind him, Nastya uses a collective numeral with the genitive plural of children.
Настя, мне этот сон совсем не понравился!
'Nastya, I did not like that dream at all!' Startled, Kostya immediately backpedals using a negated masculine past reflexive verb. Let's hear the bar conversation again from beginning to end.

Trying to cover for himself in front of Nastya, Kostya awkwardly claims that he hated his dream and couldn't wait to wake up. Listen for the verbs meaning to love, to deceive, and to wake up. See you in the next scene.
